summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In the Interest of SRS and LS
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the change of permanency plan from reunification to adoption, holding that parents are not entitled to an indefinite period to complete a case plan and that the juvenile court did not abuse its discretion in finding adoption served the children's best interests after eighteen months of limited progress.
key_cases.relevance: States the point at which a reunification plan may be abandoned notwithstanding some parental progress.
key_cases.quote: Parents are not afforded an indefinite period to achieve their case plan goals

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Termination of Parental Rights to ALRW
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 14-2-309(a)(iii), holding that the sufficiency of the Department's reasonable efforts is assessed case by case and that the Department must tie its efforts to the reasons that necessitated the child's out-of-home placement.
key_cases.relevance: Defines the reasonable-efforts showing the State must make before reunification may be abandoned.
key_cases.quote: We assess whether sufficient evidence supports that DFS made reasonable efforts to rehabilitate the family on a case-by-case basis

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Termination of Parental Rights to PML and EGL
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination, holding that whether the Department made reasonable efforts is assessed case by case, that its efforts must be accessible and tailored to the parent, and that a case plan adapted to a mother's intellectual disability satisfied the standard.
key_cases.relevance: Marks the point at which reasonable but unsuccessful efforts justify ending reunification.
key_cases.quote: We assess on a case-by-case basis whether sufficient evidence exists to demonstrate the Department made reasonable efforts to rehabilitate the family

key_cases.case_name: ARC v. State, Department of Family Services
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination, holding the Department proved by clear and convincing evidence that it made reasonable rehabilitative efforts, and that under strict scrutiny the State must use the least intrusive means, though the Court did not decide whether guardianship is a less intrusive alternative to termination.
key_cases.relevance: Fixes the evidentiary showing required before reunification efforts may be declared unsuccessful.
key_cases.quote: the district court properly concluded that DFS presented clear and convincing evidence it made reasonable efforts to reunite her with the children

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the change of the permanency plan from family reunification to adoption, holding that the State must prove the grounds for a change of permanency plan by a preponderance of the evidence and that the mother's repeated failures to appear for and to pass drug testing satisfied that burden.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes the burden and the procedural protections that apply at the precise point a reunification plan is abandoned for another permanency goal.
key_cases.quote: when a change in the permanency plan is sought, the burden upon the State is to prove grounds for that change by a preponderance of the evidence

key_cases.case_name: RH v. State, Department of Family Services (In re DRS)
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed orders placing the children with their grandparents and their father rather than returning them to the mother, holding that whether the Department made reasonable efforts is determined case by case and that the record supplied sufficient evidence of efforts to prevent removal and of the children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: A practitioner contesting whether the Department did enough before reunification was abandoned cites this case for the governing standard rather than only its later restatements.
key_cases.quote: Reasonable efforts are determined on a case-by-case basis.

state_agency.name: Wyoming Department of Family Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the DFS field office in the county where the child lives — the list is at dfs.wyo.gov/about/contact-us

extended_foster_care_age: Ends at 18; to 19 only if graduating (Wyo. DFS IV-E policy); court may order care or transitional services to 21 (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-431(b))

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
